elements.element: Customer owns all Deliverables created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 states that Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer.

elements.element: Customer owns all work product created for Customer, whether or not categorized as a Deliverable.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 covers only defined Deliverables; no operative language assigns other work product created for Customer.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 contains an express present assignment of all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in all other work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The assignment is limited to Deliverables and does not expressly cover other work product.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Sections 1.8 and 14.3 define Vendor Technology to include Vendor's pre-existing technology and provide that Vendor retains it.

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to Vendor intellectual property embedded in a Deliverable.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 applies Section 13.2's licence to Vendor Technology incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 expressly makes the applicable licence perpetual.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 expressly makes the applicable licence irrevocable.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 expressly makes the applicable licence royalty-free and fully paid.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 states that Customer owns all Customer Data and grants Vendor only a limited processing right for specified purposes.

elements.element: No intellectual property is jointly owned.
elements.evidence: Section 14.4 prevents joint ownership by default but expressly permits it through a separate signed instrument, so the prohibition is not absolute.

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools.
elements.evidence: Vendor retains pre-existing tools and modifications that are not Deliverables, but Section 14.2 assigns every Deliverable to Customer; the language does not preserve Vendor ownership of all generic tools, including tools created as Deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor owns generic know-how.
elements.evidence: Neither Section 1.8 nor Section 14.3 expressly reserves generic know-how to Vendor.

elements.element: Customer may use the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Customer's exclusive ownership and receipt of all right, title, and interest under Section 14.2 confer the right to use the Deliverables.

elements.element: Customer may modify the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Customer's unrestricted exclusive ownership under Section 14.2 confers the right to modify the Deliverables.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: As exclusive owner of all right, title, and interest, Customer may authorize third parties to use the Deliverables.

elements.element: Customer's rights in the Deliverables are perpetual.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 transfers ownership without a term limit, which is more durable than a perpetual licence.

elements.element: Customer's rights in the Deliverables are irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The present assignment in Section 14.2 contains no revocation right or termination trigger.

elements.element: Customer's rights in the Deliverables are worldwide.
elements.evidence: The assignment of all right, title, and interest is not territorially limited.

elements.element: Customer's rights in the Deliverables are royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 imposes no royalty or continuing payment condition on Customer's ownership.

elements.element: Customer may exercise its rights in the Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Customer's ownership is unrestricted and therefore permits use, modification, and third-party authorization for its business.

result.reason: The redline clearly reverses Deliverable ownership and preserves Vendor Technology, Customer Data ownership, and the embedded-technology licence. It does not expressly capture non-Deliverable work product, and the joint-ownership provision contains an exception. The fallback is also incomplete because Vendor ownership of all generic tools and know-how is not secured. The amendment is targeted and does not disturb unrelated terms, but it does not reach a complete preferred or fallback level.
